question: Your developer productivity agent builds change timelines for engineers who explore a legacy system. It calls an MCP issue tracker tool that returns Unix timestamps and an MCP git history tool that returns ISO 8601 strings. A colleague wrote a hook that converts Unix timestamps to ISO 8601 and registered it to intercept outgoing tool calls. The agent still receives raw Unix timestamps and orders events wrongly. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The hook intercepts outgoing tool calls, so it runs before the issue tracker tool returns any result that it could convert.
options.reason: Interception of outgoing calls acts before any result exists. The guide uses PostToolUse hooks to transform tool results before the model processes them.

options.text: The issue tracker server is missing from the .mcp.json configuration, so the hook never receives any tool results from that MCP server to act on.
options.reason: The agent receives Unix timestamps from the issue tracker tool, so the server is configured and returns results. The fault is the hook type, which runs on outgoing calls.

options.text: Agent SDK hooks can only observe tool results for logging, so they cannot change the data that the model receives from MCP tools.
options.reason: The guide states that PostToolUse hooks intercept tool results and transform them before the model processes them, so hooks can change that data.

options.text: The system prompt of the agent does not tell the agent that a hook has already converted the timestamps to ISO 8601 for it.
options.reason: A hook transformation is deterministic and does not depend on prompt instructions. The agent also sees raw timestamps, so no conversion has happened that the prompt could describe.
